symptom: Studio Pro 11.12.2 rebase/merge throws `Objects with ID … of type DomainModels$AccessRule do not have the same properties. baseNames = MemberAccesses, AllowedModuleRoles, AllowCreate, AllowDelete, DefaultMemberAccessRights, XPathConstraint; newNames = AllowCreate, AllowDelete, AllowedModuleRoles, DefaultMemberAccessRights, Documentation, MemberAccesses, XPathConstraint, XPathConstraintCaption` for a user on mxcli 0.26, and the project then does not open (Studio Pro re-runs the unfinished merge on open). Suspected first: a remote change made with 11.15
cause: The merge base is a revision an mxcli before 0.26 wrote (mendixlabs/mxcli#1373, fixed in 0.26.0): a NEW access rule without Documentation and XPathConstraintCaption. The local branch's Studio Pro save wrote the full set, and MergeLib compares the base against each side by property names. Upgrading mxcli or running `fix property-sets` fixes only revisions from that commit on: a merge whose base predates it fails on every document that was incomplete in the base and that both branches changed. Measured with `mx merge`: a repaired side against the old base is still exit 129; with the repaired revision as the base it is exit 0
file: docs only: `docs-site/src/tools/outside-studio-pro.md` ('The repair reaches forward, not back' and the recovery steps), `cmd/mxcli/cmd_fix_property_sets.go` (Long help). The writer fix itself is `modelsdk/canon/propertyset.go` + `modelsdk/canon/studiopro_property_defaults.json` (rows DomainModels$AccessRule Documentation / XPathConstraintCaption)
insight: **The key ORDER in baseNames/newNames names the writer**: MergeLib prints names in stored order. Studio Pro stores them alphabetically (= newNames); mxcli in the gen metamodel order (`modelsdk/gen/<domain>/types.go` init) minus the keys it omitted, and a v0.25.0 build's `grant` on a new rule wrote exactly the reported baseNames. Build the suspect release in a worktree and dump the keys instead of reasoning from the changelog. **Only elements old mxcli CREATED are incomplete** (new entity + grant, or grant for a role with no rule yet): modifying a Studio Pro rule or rewriting the domain model kept the keys (measured). When old mxcli also created the entity, `mx diff` names the EntityImpl (Image/ImageData/Source) before the rule, so an AccessRule in the report points at a grant onto a Studio Pro entity. **The table rules out a version mismatch**: the AccessRule set is identical from 10.24.24 to 11.15.0. **`mx merge BASE MINE THEIRS` reproduces Studio Pro's merge headlessly** ('Exception during merging', exit 129), with the three trees from `git archive`. **The recovery that works**: on your branch, put the units that were incomplete in the base and that both branches changed back to the merge base (`git checkout <base> -- <unit>`, then `fix hashes --repair`, because the .mpr Unit table indexes ContentsHash), merge rather than rebase (a rebase replays the earlier commits that changed the unit), and redo the edits. Result: mx merge exit 0, mx check identical to the untouched fixture. Taking one side of the conflicted files at git level does NOT work in general: the .mpr conflicts too, as a binary file that indexes every unit, and either side drops the other's unit rows
